sources.title: Batch 0059 frozen Redis/MySQL consistency source context

claims.text: The frozen source Questions ask how to keep Redis cache consistent with an authoritative database/MySQL and explicitly preserve delayed double-delete and Canal as interview entities; the source does not provide production QPS, topology, SLO or incident metrics.

Redis and MySQL do not share an automatic cross-store atomic transaction; the candidate therefore defines the database as authoritative, uses cache-aside with database-first invalidation for the default path, and treats TTL as stale-lifetime bounding rather than a correctness proof.

Delayed double-delete is presented as a best-effort mitigation for the old-read refill race, with the delay derived from observed latency and the second delete still requiring reliable retry/repair; it is not presented as a strong-consistency guarantee.

The Canal/binlog path is described as asynchronous repair from committed database change facts, with checkpoint, replay, idempotency, log-retention and stale-event boundaries; refresh events require a version/change-position rule so late events cannot regress cache state.

The scenario explicitly separates illustrative capacity/SLO assumptions from source facts and requires retry, lag/oldest-event monitoring, reconciliation, fault injection and a stricter read-after-write path when ordinary eventual consistency is insufficient.
